title: Kaiser Marshall, Walter Johnson, Sonny Greer and Ray McKinley
summary: Jones compares Kaiser Marshall, Walter Johnson ("Mr. Drums"), Sonny Greer and Ray McKinley, favoring Johnson's finesse and McKinley's cleanness.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I want to ask you - when I came in which is around your time too, maybe a day or so before, the first great drummer that I had really heard that was exciting, like you, was a fellow named Kaiser Marshall. Do you remember Kaiser, Jo?

Yes, but Kaiser was exciting but he became mechanical to hang out with the drummer of the day before Gene Krupa and it didn't make any sense. But see, Mr. Drums - I had a picture that I should have brought out here - his name is That's Mr. Walter Johnson, Mr. Drums. I call Sonny Greer "Empire State Building" but Mr. Drums the epitome of the finesse,
because when he joined Fletcher he took Kaiser's place but the clique didn't like Walter but Walter was the better drummer.
Who did he join - whose band was that?
Fletcher Henderson. They got rid of him and got Kaiser back. Coleman told Fletcher, "You should have kept the boy because he doesn't play as much as Walter."
You say you called Sonny Greer - the great Sonny Greer with Duke Ellington -
Empire State Building, that's the big one, huh?
That's the only drum stylist that I've ever seen in my life. He's a stylist, you see what I mean, to play these effects and things. You don't get that, you see, that calls for a whole lot of living.
In your travels you must have run into at some time or another, into Ray McKinley. Do you remember Ray McKinley?

Incidentally, he did "Parade of the Milk Bottle Caps" of which I have the record. There has never been a cleaner solo in life. But I knew the Texan and this Texan said, "I'm going to sing." I said, "What are you going to sing for?" So he started to sing one of these hillbilly things he did. I said, "Man, don't sing," so he started singing. But he was the cleanest drummer, you know,
